description: MUST-FAIL: digest_alg inconsistent with the referenced artifact type's registered canonicalization context. The typed reference carries the correct SHA-256 digest for the cited artifact under its jcs-n/authorization-doc context, but labels digest_alg with a hash algorithm other than the one that context actually uses. A verifier that recomputes and compares the digest bytes without independently confirming digest_alg would find the comparison succeeds and wrongly accept the reference.
spec_ref: draft-mih-sokolov-scitt-payload-binding-01 §7.1 ('It MUST use the `type` field to resolve the referenced artifact's registered digest context. It MUST confirm that `digest_alg` identifies a hash algorithm consistent with that context. It MUST then recompute the referenced artifact's digest under that context and compare the recomputed value with the value carried in the `digest` field.') together with §13.1 (Canonicalization Algorithm Registry: jcs-n's registered hash algorithm is SHA-256).

registry_entry.name: authorization-doc
registry_entry.digest_context: jcs-n; exclusion set {doc_id}; hash algorithm SHA-256 (per the jcs-n Algorithm Registry entry); 64-char lowercase hex

typed_references_with_mislabeled_digest_.note: Names a different, longer-digest hash algorithm; the carried digest is still the correct 32-byte SHA-256 value.
Names a hash algorithm with a shorter native digest; the carried digest is still the correct SHA-256 value.
Names a string that identifies no hash algorithm in any registry.
The empty string is not a valid hash-algorithm identifier.

verification.note: For every example above, the carried digest equals correct_recomputed_digest, so a verifier that only performs recompute-and-compare (skipping the digest_alg check) would find step 4's comparison succeeds and wrongly accept the reference. §7.1 requires confirming digest_alg is consistent with the registered context's hash algorithm (SHA-256) BEFORE relying on that comparison. A conforming verifier MUST reject digest_alg values that do not name 'SHA-256' (case-insensitive) for a jcs-n-context reference, regardless of whether the carried digest bytes are otherwise correct.
verification.result: FAIL (for each of the four digest_alg examples above)

provenance: Locally authored to close a revision-uplift gap: an earlier state of this library bound digest_alg into TypedRef without validating it, so SHA-512, MD5, an unregistered name, and the empty string were all wrongly accepted against a jcs-n entry as long as the carried digest bytes were correct. This vector is not a fold of any external vector file; no external source file has been verified for this vector.
